packages.name: jq
packages.synopsis: Package jq is a standard-library-only implementation of the jq query language (jqlang/jq 1.7 semantics).
packages.doc:
Package jq is a standard-library-only implementation of the jq query
language (jqlang/jq 1.7 semantics).

# Overview

A jq program is a filter: it takes one JSON value as input and produces a
stream of zero or more JSON values as output. Every expression in the
language is such a generator, and the whole evaluator is built around that
idea — Query.RunFunc pushes each output to a callback as it is produced, so
"empty" yields nothing, "1,2,3" yields three values, and "first(range(1e9))"
stops after the first. There are no third-party dependencies and no cgo.

# Values

Values are ordinary Go values: nil for JSON null, bool, float64 for every
number, string, []any for arrays, and map[string]any for objects. Unmarshal
decodes JSON into that shape and Marshal encodes it back, using jq's own
number formatting (integral values print without a trailing ".0") and jq's
string escaping. Object key order is not preserved; keys are emitted sorted,
so keys and keys_unsorted return the same thing.

# Running a program

	q, err := jq.Compile(".users[] | select(.age > 30) | .name")
	out, err := q.Run(input)

	// or, in one call:
	out, err := jq.Eval(".a.b", map[string]any{"a": map[string]any{"b": 1}})

Query.WithVariables binds values a program can reach as $name, and
Query.RunFunc streams results, stopping as soon as the callback returns an
error. A compiled Query is immutable and safe for concurrent use.

# Language support

The implementation covers the core language: identity, field, index, slice
and iteration (including the optional forms ".a?" and ".[]?"), pipe, comma,
the alternative operator "//", arithmetic and comparison, and/or/not,
if/then/elif/else/end, try/catch and the postfix "?", reduce and foreach,
"as" bindings with array and object destructuring (including the "?//"
alternative patterns), label/break, user-defined functions with filter
arguments and closures, string interpolation, the @base64, @base64d, @csv,
@tsv, @html, @uri, @json, @sh and @text format strings (also usable as
interpolation prefixes, as in @base64 "x=\(.x)"), object and array
construction, recursive descent (".." and recurse), path expressions
(path, getpath, setpath, delpaths, paths, leaf_paths, del) and every
assignment operator: =, |=, +=, -=, *=, /=, %= and //=.

Path expressions are first class: an expression is evaluated together with
the location it came from, so "path(.a[0].b)" reports ["a",0,"b"] and
"(.a,.b) |= .+1" updates both locations. An expression that does not denote a
location, such as "path(1+1)", fails with a runtime error.

Most builtins that jq itself writes in jq — map, select, recurse, to_entries,
first, limit, until, walk, paths, del and the rest — are likewise defined in
jq here (see the package's prelude), which is what makes them behave
correctly inside path expressions and as generators.

# Regular expressions

test, match, capture, scan, sub, gsub, split/2 and splits use the standard
library's regexp package, which implements RE2. RE2 guarantees linear-time
matching, but unlike the Oniguruma engine that jq links against it does not
support backreferences or lookaround assertions; programs using those
constructs fail with a runtime error rather than matching. The "g", "i", "x",
"n", "s", "m" and "p" flags are honoured. This is a deliberate, documented
parity gap.

# Bounded evaluation

jq programs can diverge — "repeat(.)" and "recurse(.+1)" never terminate. A
Query therefore carries a step budget (DefaultMaxSteps) and a nesting depth
limit (DefaultMaxDepth); exceeding either fails with ErrStepLimit, which the
program's own try/catch cannot intercept. Query.WithMaxSteps raises, lowers
or disables the budget. A caller that wants full control can instead run with
no budget and stop iteration from RunFunc.

# Errors

Compile failures are *CompileError and match errors.Is(err, jq.ErrCompile).
Failures raised while running — type errors from operators and builtins, and
values raised by the program's own error/0 and error/1 — are *RuntimeError
and match errors.Is(err, jq.ErrRuntime); type errors additionally match
jq.ErrType, and RuntimeError.Value returns the raw value carried by error/1.
A step budget overrun is ErrStepLimit and an escaped break is ErrBreak.

# Known differences from upstream jq

  - Object key order is not preserved (Go maps are unordered).
  - Numbers are float64 throughout; jq 1.7 preserves the literal text of
    numbers that pass through a program unchanged, and this port does not.
  - JSON input must be strict: the non-standard nan, NaN and Infinity
    literals that jq's own parser accepts are rejected by Unmarshal.
  - Modules (import, include, modulemeta) and the streaming builtins are not
    implemented.
  - Regular expressions are RE2, as described above.

This package is a re-implementation, not a binding, and is not affiliated
with the jq project.

consts.doc:
DefaultMaxDepth bounds how deeply expressions may nest at run time, which
keeps a runaway recursive definition from exhausting the goroutine stack
before the step budget notices.

DefaultMaxSteps is the number of evaluation steps a Query is allowed to take
before it fails with ErrStepLimit. It bounds otherwise non-terminating
programs such as "repeat(.)" or "recurse(.+1)". Change it per query with
Query.WithMaxSteps.

vars.doc:
Sentinel errors returned by the package. Every error produced by Compile,
Eval, Query.Run and Query.RunFunc wraps one of these, so callers can classify
a failure with errors.Is without type-asserting the concrete error value.

types.name: CompileError
types.doc:
CompileError reports a program that could not be parsed or compiled. Offset
is the byte offset into Program at which the problem was detected, or -1 when
no position is available.

methods.name: Is
methods.doc: Is reports whether the error matches ErrCompile or ErrSyntax.

methods.name: Unwrap
methods.doc: Unwrap reports ErrCompile so that errors.Is(err, jq.ErrCompile) matches.

types.name: Query
types.doc:
Query is a compiled jq program. A Query is immutable and safe for concurrent
use by multiple goroutines; the option methods return a modified copy.

funcs.name: Compile
funcs.doc:
Compile parses and compiles a jq program. The returned *Query may be run any
number of times, against any number of inputs. Syntax errors and references
to undefined functions or variables are reported as *CompileError, which
matches errors.Is(err, jq.ErrCompile).

funcs.name: MustCompile
funcs.doc:
MustCompile is like Compile but panics if the program does not compile. It
is intended for package-level variables holding known-good programs.

methods.name: Run
methods.doc: Run executes the program against input and collects every output value.

methods.name: RunFunc
methods.signature: func (q *Query) RunFunc(input any, fn func(any) error) error
methods.doc:
RunFunc executes the program against input, calling fn once for every output
value in order. If fn returns a non-nil error, iteration stops and that error
is returned unchanged, which lets a caller take the first N results or impose
its own deadline on a long-running program.

Errors raised by the program itself are returned as *RuntimeError; a step
budget overrun is returned as ErrStepLimit.

methods.name: String
methods.doc: String returns the program text the Query was compiled from.

methods.name: WithMaxSteps
methods.doc:
WithMaxSteps returns a copy of q with a different evaluation step budget. A
value of zero or less disables the budget entirely, in which case the caller
is responsible for stopping runaway programs from RunFunc.

methods.name: WithVariables
methods.doc:
WithVariables returns a copy of q in which the given names are bound as jq
variables, so a program may refer to them as $name. The values must be jq
values (nil, bool, float64, string, []any or map[string]any).

types.name: RuntimeError
types.doc:
RuntimeError reports a failure raised while a program was running: a type
error from an operator or builtin, or an uncaught value raised by the
program's own error/0 or error/1 builtin.

methods.name: Is
methods.doc:
Is reports whether the error matches ErrRuntime, or ErrType when the failure
was caused by a value of the wrong type.

methods.name: Unwrap
methods.doc: Unwrap reports ErrRuntime so that errors.Is(err, jq.ErrRuntime) matches.

methods.name: Value
methods.doc:
Value returns the jq value carried by the program's error/1 builtin and
whether one was present. Errors raised inside this package report false.

funcs.name: Eval
funcs.signature: func Eval(program string, input any) ([]any, error)
funcs.doc:
Eval compiles program and runs it against input in one call, returning every
output value the program produces.

funcs.name: Marshal
funcs.doc:
Marshal encodes v as compact, jq-compatible JSON. Numbers use jq's shortest
round-trip formatting (integral values print without a trailing ".0"), object
keys are emitted in sorted order, and HTML-significant characters are not
escaped. NaN encodes as null and infinities clamp to the largest finite
double, as in jq.

A value nested deeper than jq's own MAX_PRINT_DEPTH is not descended into:
the sub-value is replaced by the JSON string "<skipped: too deep>", exactly as
jq's printer does, so the result is still valid JSON. See limits.go.

funcs.name: Unmarshal
funcs.doc:
Unmarshal decodes JSON the way jq does: objects become map[string]any, arrays
become []any, numbers become float64, strings become string, and JSON null
becomes the untyped Go nil. Key order is not preserved.

A leading UTF-8 byte order mark is ignored, matching jq's tolerance of BOMs
in input files.

Input nested deeper than jq's own MAX_PARSING_DEPTH (10000 containers) is
rejected rather than decoded, so that a hostile document cannot exhaust
memory in the decoder. See limits.go.
